title: Site and speed
purpose: When a shopper taps an ad on a phone on a slow connection and the product will not show, open Site and speed to get the product in front of them fast, and see it pay off in bounce and mobile conversion.
fires: The yearly speed agency audit, the speed score screenshot, the developer's 'it is fast on my machine', and the habit of blaming the ads when mobile sales slip.
not_for: A store whose key pages already show the product fast on real phones and whose mobile conversion sits close to desktop; speed work there buys little.

jobs.job: When a shopper taps our ad on a phone on a slow connection and the product image will not load, get the product and price on screen in under 2.5 seconds, so I stop paying for clicks that leave before they see what they came for
jobs.circumstance: Evening; a shopper on a mid-range phone with a patchy signal taps an ad, stares at a grey box for 4 seconds, and taps back

progress.functional: the main product image and price show fast on a real phone, starting with the pages ads land on
progress.emotional: stop the gut feeling that paid clicks vanish before they see the product
progress.social: show the agency and the team that the page is not why ads fail

jobs.hire_today: a speed agency once a year, a developer when asked, or nothing
jobs.fire: the yearly audit and the speed score screenshot

forces.push: paid mobile bounce is 64 percent on the top product page
forces.pull: what a shopper on a slow phone sees, second by second, and the one fix that shows the product sooner
forces.habit: the site looks fast on my office wifi
forces.anxiety: what if the fix breaks the page or makes the photos look worse

jobs.little_hire: weekly, and whenever paid mobile bounce jumps

watch.metric: time until the main product image shows, mobile, slowest 1 in 4 real visits, 28 days, top ad landing pages
watch.source: Chrome real-user data via PageSpeed Insights and Search Console, plus lab runs on a throttled mid-range phone profile, 3 runs averaged

drives.metric: paid mobile bounce rate on those pages, 28 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the top product page shows its image at 4.1 seconds and paid mobile bounce is 64 percent. After: 2.3 seconds and 55 percent, once 28 days of real visits land.
jobs.not_for: a store whose ad landing pages already show the product in under 2.5 seconds on real phones

jobs.job: When mobile bounce jumps or mobile conversion drops this week, tell me whether the site got slower before we blame the ads, so I fix the right thing
jobs.circumstance: Monday; mobile conversion fell from 1.4 to 1.1 percent, and the media buyer says the ads are tired

progress.functional: a yes or no on whether key pages got slower, with the date and the cause
progress.social: settle it with the media buyer and the agency using a picture, not an opinion

jobs.hire_today: the media buyer's guess, or nothing
jobs.fire: the argument, and fixes aimed at the wrong thing

forces.push: a week of wrong fixes while sales slip
forces.pull: page speed by day next to bounce and conversion, with every site change marked
forces.anxiety: what if speed and ads both moved and it cannot split them

jobs.little_hire: whenever mobile bounce or conversion moves more than a few points

watch.metric: load time on key pages by day, against mobile bounce, 14 days
watch.source: scheduled lab runs and GA4

drives.metric: mobile conversion rate, 7 days, against the 28 day average

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 weeks blaming the ads for a drop caused by a 900 KB review widget. After: the cause named the same day.
jobs.not_for: a store with so little mobile traffic that weekly swings are noise

jobs.job: When a developer delays or moves scripts to speed up the site, check the Meta pixel and GA4 still count purchases, so I do not let ads learn from bad data
jobs.circumstance: A script delay went live Tuesday; by Thursday Meta shows 30 percent fewer purchases than Shopify

progress.functional: every purchase event still fires after each speed change
progress.emotional: stop the fear that speed work quietly breaks the ads

jobs.fire: shipping speed changes with no tracking check

forces.push: ads optimize on missing purchases and costs rise
forces.pull: a tracking check built into every speed change
forces.habit: speed and tracking are different people's jobs
forces.anxiety: what if the check needs a real purchase every time

jobs.little_hire: after every script or loading change

watch.metric: purchases counted by Meta against Shopify orders, 7 days
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager and Shopify orders

drives.metric: cost per purchase, 7 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: after a script delay Meta counts 61 percent of orders, down from 88. After: back to 88 percent within 1 day.
jobs.not_for: a store that runs no paid ads

jobs.job: When the team uploads camera-size photos every week, stop new heavy images from undoing the speed work, without making the product look worse, so I keep the pages fast as the catalog grows
jobs.circumstance: A 6 MB lifestyle photo went on the home page this morning; nobody on the content team knows it matters

progress.functional: every new image sized and squeezed before it goes live, with no visible loss
progress.emotional: stop watching speed gains leak away

jobs.hire_today: nothing; the designer does not know it matters
jobs.fire: uploading straight from the camera roll

forces.push: a single photo can add 2 seconds on a phone
forces.pull: a daily sweep that names each heavy image, its page and the fixed size
forces.habit: the platform shrinks images for us
forces.anxiety: what if squeezing makes the product look cheap

watch.metric: image weight on the 5 key page types, latest run
watch.source: lab runs on a throttled mid-range phone profile, 3 runs averaged

drives.metric: time until the main image shows, mobile, 28 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the product page loads 3,800 KB of images, one at 1,900 KB. After: 900 KB with no visible loss; the image shows 1.2 seconds sooner in the lab the same day.
jobs.not_for: a store whose images go through a developer who already sizes every file

watch.metric: load time and page weight against each page type's limit, checked after every change
